title: UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration — principles for effective restoration
claim: Effective ecosystem restoration prioritises native species matched to local site conditions and requires baseline and follow-up monitoring to confirm that interventions are producing measurable ecological change.
evidence_text: The UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration's ten restoration principles emphasise using native, locally-sourced species matched to site-specific soil, salinity, and hydrological conditions rather than generic planting, and stress that restoration outcomes must be verified through baseline and follow-up ecological monitoring rather than assumed from planting activity alone. This underpins the practice of pairing any restoration action with a monitoring and reporting (MRV) process.
